canDo.en: I can talk about my life experiences and how long things have lasted, choosing between the present perfect and the past simple.
canDo.bg: Мога да говоря за преживяванията си и за това откога трае нещо, като избирам между present perfect и past simple.

title.en: Have you ever…? vs When did you…?
title.bg: Have you ever…? или When did you…?

body.en: Use the present perfect (have/has + past participle) for experiences in your life up to now, when the exact time isn't important: I've been to Rome. Have you ever tried sushi? As soon as you say or ask when it happened (in 2019, last year, two days ago, When…?), switch to the past simple: I went to Rome in 2019. Bulgarian uses the same past tense in both situations ("Ходил съм в Рим" / "Ходих в Рим миналата година"), so English learners often mix them up — the time word decides.
body.bg: Използвай present perfect (have/has + трето причастие) за преживявания в живота ти досега, когато точното време не е важно: I've been to Rome. Have you ever tried sushi? Щом кажеш или попиташ кога е станало (in 2019, last year, two days ago, When…?), минаваш на past simple: I went to Rome in 2019. На български и в двата случая използваш минало време ("Ходил съм в Рим" / "Ходих в Рим миналата година"), затова лесно се бъркат — решава думата за време.

examples: She has never driven a car.
When did you start working here?

body.en: For something that started in the past and is still true, English uses the present perfect, not the present: I've lived here for three years (not "I live here for three years"). In Bulgarian you say "Живея тук от три години" in the present, which is why this is a classic mistake. Use "for" + a period of time (for ten minutes, for ages) and "since" + the starting point (since Monday, since 2015, since I was a child).
body.bg: За нещо, което е започнало в миналото и още продължава, английският използва present perfect, а не сегашно време: I've lived here for three years (не "I live here for three years"). На български казваш "Живея тук от три години" в сегашно време — затова това е класическа грешка. "For" + период (for ten minutes, for ages), а "since" + начална точка (since Monday, since 2015, since I was a child).

examples: I've lived here for three years.
We've known each other since school.
He hasn't called me since Monday.
How long have you worked here?

texts.title: Ten years on the road
paragraphs: People often ask me how many countries I've visited. Honestly, I've never counted. I've been a travel blogger since 2015, and I've stayed in small villages and huge cities on four continents.
My first big trip was to Vietnam. I went there with a friend after university, and we spent two months travelling by train and bus. I had never eaten such amazing food before.
Have I ever been in danger? Only once. In 2019 I lost my passport in Peru and nearly missed my flight home. Luckily, a kind taxi driver found it and brought it back to my hotel.
I've lived in Lisbon for three years now, and I still haven't seen everything here. Maybe that's the best thing about travel: there's always something new.

items.prompt: You want to know if your new friend has had this experience at any time in their life. What do you ask?
options: Have you ever try Japanese food?
Are you ever trying Japanese food?
Do you ever tried Japanese food?
Have you ever tried Japanese food?

explanation.en: For experiences at any time up to now, the question is "Have you ever + past participle?": tried, not try. "Do you ever tried" mixes present and past, and "Are you ever trying" is about habits now, not life experience.
explanation.bg: За опит в който и да е момент досега въпросът е "Have you ever + трето причастие?": tried, а не try. "Do you ever tried" смесва сегашно и минало, а "Are you ever trying" е за навици сега, не за житейски опит.

hints.en: Which tense connects the past with now?
hints.bg: Кое време свързва миналото със сега?

objective.en: Use the past simple with a finished time.
objective.bg: Да използваш past simple с приключило време.

items.sentence: I ___ (go) to Japan in 2019, and I loved it.

explanation.en: "In 2019" is a finished time, so we need the past simple: went. "I've been to Japan in 2019" is wrong — the present perfect can't go with a specific past time.
explanation.bg: "In 2019" е приключило време, затова трябва past simple: went. "I've been to Japan in 2019" е грешно — present perfect не може с конкретно минало време.

hints.en: Is there a time word that tells you when?
hints.bg: Има ли дума, която казва кога?

objective.en: Use "for" with a period of time.
objective.bg: Да използваш "for" с период от време.

items.sentence: My brother has worked at the bank ___ six years.

explanation.en: "Six years" is a length of time, so we use "for". "Since" needs a starting point: since 2019. Bulgarian "от" covers both, which is why learners say "since six years" by mistake.
explanation.bg: "Six years" е продължителност, затова използваме "for". "Since" изисква начална точка: since 2019. Българското "от" покрива и двете, затова често се греши "since six years".

hints.en: Is "six years" a period or a starting point?
hints.bg: "Six years" период ли е, или начална точка?

items.sentence: It has rained every day ___ Monday.

explanation.en: "Monday" is the moment when the rain started, so we use "since". With a length of time (four days) you would use "for".
explanation.bg: "Monday" е моментът, в който е започнал дъждът, затова използваме "since". С продължителност (four days) би било "for".

objective.en: Avoid the present tense for duration up to now.
objective.bg: Да избягваш сегашно време за продължителност досега.

items.prompt: You moved to Sofia in 2020 and you still live there. Which sentence is correct?
options: I am living in Sofia since 2020.

explanation.en: Something that started in the past and continues now needs the present perfect: I've lived in Sofia since 2020. In Bulgarian "Живея в София от 2020" is present, but English doesn't allow the present with "since". "I lived" would mean you don't live there any more — and then "since" doesn't work.
explanation.bg: Нещо, което е започнало в миналото и продължава сега, изисква present perfect: I've lived in Sofia since 2020. На български "Живея в София от 2020" е сегашно време, но английският не допуска сегашно време със "since". "I lived" би значело, че вече не живееш там — и тогава "since" не пасва.

hints.en: Do you still live there? Which tense joins past and present?
hints.bg: Още ли живееш там? Кое време свързва минало и настояще?

objective.en: Ask how long a situation has lasted.

accept: How long have you known Elena?

explanation.en: To ask about duration up to now: How long + have/has + subject + past participle? Bulgarian says "Откога познаваш Елена?" in the present, but English needs "have you known".
explanation.bg: За да попиташ за продължителност досега: How long + have/has + подлог + трето причастие? На български "Откога познаваш Елена?" е в сегашно време, а на английски трябва "have you known".

objective.en: Say you have never done something.
objective.bg: Да кажеш, че никога не си правил нещо.

explanation.en: "Never" goes between "have" and the past participle: I've never been… Notice "been to" (gone and come back), not "gone to". Also, English uses only one negative: "I've never been", not "I haven't never been" — unlike Bulgarian "никога не съм ходил".
explanation.bg: "Never" стои между "have" и третото причастие: I've never been… Обърни внимание: "been to" (ходил и върнал се), а не "gone to". И в английския има само едно отрицание: "I've never been", а не "I haven't never been" — за разлика от "никога не съм ходил".

items.prompt: What do we know about the writer and Lisbon?
options: The writer visited Lisbon for three years and then left.
The writer has never been to Lisbon.
The writer moved to Lisbon three years ago and still lives there.
The writer lived in Lisbon before 2015.

explanation.en: "I've lived in Lisbon for three years now" — the present perfect with "for… now" means it started three years ago and is still true.
explanation.bg: "I've lived in Lisbon for three years now" — present perfect с "for… now" значи, че е започнало преди три години и още е вярно.

hints.en: Look at the tense in the last paragraph.

objective.en: Notice why a text uses the past simple.
objective.bg: Да забележиш защо текстът използва past simple.

items.prompt: Why does the writer say "In 2019 I lost my passport" and not "In 2019 I've lost my passport"?
options: Because the sentence gives a finished time, so the past simple is needed.
Because the passport is still lost.
Because it happened more than once.

explanation.en: "In 2019" is a specific finished time, and the present perfect can't be used with it. The passport was found, and it happened only once, so the other answers are wrong.
explanation.bg: "In 2019" е конкретно приключило време и present perfect не може да се използва с него. Паспортът е намерен и се е случило само веднъж, така че другите отговори са грешни.

hints.en: Look at the first two words of the sentence.
hints.bg: Виж първите две думи в изречението.

objective.en: Find a detail in a blog post.
objective.bg: Да намериш подробност в блог пост.
